info.name: Smart Job Tracker
info.description:
Hand-maintained happy-path and error flows for the Smart Job Tracker backend.

This collection is deliberately NOT an exhaustive endpoint list. The generated OpenAPI document at {{baseUrl}}/v3/api-docs is the exhaustive list, and it cannot drift from the controllers. Import that when you want every endpoint with every field.

What lives here instead is the part a spec cannot express: ordered flows that chain one response into the next request, and assertions that pin the API contract.

Select the 'Smart Job Tracker - Local' environment before running. Run the 'Jobs' folder with the Collection Runner to execute the full create-read-update-delete cycle in order. Run the 'Tasks', 'Notes', or 'Timeline' folder the same way for a job's tasks, notes, or timeline; each seeds its own job rather than depending on the 'Jobs' folder having run first.

header.description: Browsers attach Origin to every non-GET request, same-origin ones included. Newman does not, so without this line no run here can see a CORS mapping refusing the app's own writes.

  "location": "Remote",

  "source": "LINKEDIN",

  "salaryMin": 90000.00,

  "description": "Build and maintain backend services."
}

request.description:
Every field is optional except company and roleTitle. Omitting status defaults it to WISHLIST in CreateJobCommand rather than in the request DTO.

This request sends an Origin header, as Update job and Delete job do, and it is not decoration. A browser sends Origin on every write, so a CORS mapping that does not list the app's own origin answers 403 to all of them while reads keep working. That defect shipped through three tasks because nothing here, and no curl check, sent the header. All three writes carry it because a mapping can restrict methods as well as origins, which would break edit and delete while leaving create working. See docs/engineering/same-origin-api-boundary.md.

exec: pm.test('the backend applied no CORS processing', function () {
'a 403 here means a CORS mapping is refusing the origin the app is served '
+ 'from, so every browser write fails while reads keep working. See '
'an allow-origin header means a CORS mapping exists. Allowing this origin '
+ 'explicitly, or allowing every origin, both answer the symptom instead of '
+ 'removing the check, and the second opens the API to any site.',
